Coding accessibility: Software by the blind, for the blind
recent_posts.summary: An article about coding accessibility, focusing on NVDA, an open source screen reader for blind and low-vision individuals. It explores how NVDA empowers the blind community, encourages blind developers, and improves accessibility in various aspects of life.

recent_posts.title: Coding accessibility: How Della found her voice with open source AAC
recent_posts.summary: Della Calder, who had been in speech therapy for a few years, struggled to find an app that resonated with her. Her brother, Archer, built an open source AAC app called FreeSpeech specifically tailored to her needs and preferences. The app allows users to communicate by pushing individual buttons for words and ideas, translating them to speech. Della's involvement in the development process has been crucial, inspiring the initial design and contributing to a more accessible and usable product. FreeSpeech has enabled Della to participate in the world where other proprietary AAC apps failed.

recent_posts.title: Scaling standards and community in your organization
recent_posts.summary: Leaders must enable agility across their team’s technical capabilities. The foundation for this kind of agility, across any size organization, begins with a culture built on continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and a passion for innovation. In this Guide, you will learn: How to scale adoption of engineering best practices and organizational standards.

recent_posts.title: Treat accessibility issues as bugs, not feature requests
recent_posts.summary: accessibility issues are a never-ending list of problems. Treat accessibility issues as bugs, not feature requests, says Drupal Core Accessibility Maintainer Dries Buytaert. Drupal has been a leader in digital accessibility for over a decade now.

recent_posts.title: Provisioning self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on demand
recent_posts.summary: Philips scaled its GitHub self-hosted runners in the cloud to enable CI/CD for the enterprise. The solution is open source and easy to deploy using Terraform and GitHub Actions for automation. In this video Guide, you will learn how Philips' software development process operates and why control over systems is crucial.

recent_posts.title: Anton Mirhorodchenko
recent_posts.summary: Anton Mirhorodchenko was born with cerebral palsy, which made it hard for him to do things that he could see others do with relative ease. When he was 14, he learned programming could be a career, or even much sense of the other benefits it could bring. He started freelancing in 2012 after a house fire.

top_posts.title: The modern web’s underrated powerhouse
top_posts.summary: CSS is a powerful and often underrated skill for developers that plays a crucial role in shaping the modern web. It helps define the look, adaptability, usability, and accessibility of web pages. Despite its initial limitations and frustrations, CSS has evolved into a mature and robust cornerstone of web development. Open source tools and frameworks, such as Sass and Bootstrap, have made CSS development easier and more efficient. CSS specifications continue to improve with new features like Flexbox, Grid, and container queries, making CSS more adaptable and customizable.

top_posts.title: Non-code contributions are the secret to open source success
top_posts.summary: Non-code contributions are the secret to open source success, says GitHub Mathematics teacher Sarah Rainsberger. The more complex the project, the more documentation, tutorials, and support are needed to make the code useful. Easy-to-source documentation boosts productivity by about 50% in both open source and enterprise software projects.
